newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals mostly lower on strong yen.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals mostly lower on strong yen.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures, except for palladium futures, settled lower across the board on Wednesday on light volume, depressed by the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from seven to 10 yen per gram weaker, with most-active benchmark February ending down eight yen at 1,374 yen.
Bullion was quoted easier at $350.60/351.10 per ounce against $351.70/352.20 in New York on Tuesday.
"Recent falls in U.S. stock and bond markets supported bullion, but failed to boost it sharply," one trader said.
The trader said gold bullion prices are expected to remain confined to tight ranges between $349.50 and $352.50 per ounce in the near-term.

In gold futures, price losses were partly offset by short-covering, but general activity remained lacklustre partly ahead of a launch of yen-based aluminium futures contract on the TOCOM from next week.

"Trade was quiet. Commodity brokers are tending to recommend that private investors close their positions in precious metals and put their money into the newly listed aluminium futures contract," another trader said.
Platinum futures ended lower on weaker bullion prices and the yen's firmer trend, while palladium futures were up, backed by stronger bullion prices in New York overnight.
Platinum futures moved within tight ranges for most of the day before trade house selling dented prices.

Trade in palladium futures was directionless amid a lack of fresh factors. Benchmark February platinum was off nine yen at 1,446 yen, while benchmark February palladium was up three yen at 568 yen. Benchmark February silver was down 3.9 yen at 198.1 yen.
